description: Anomalousness Index rubric. Score = sum(component_value * weight), clamped 0-100. NOT a probability of extraterrestrial origin. Reflects evidentiary weight that the encounter remains unexplained after conventional analysis.

component_overrides._note: Files whose default rubric inputs would misdescribe the record. Every file not listed here uses the defaults set in pipeline/parse_csv.py. Each entry sets only the named component; all other components keep their default. Listed here so anyone recomputing the scores can reproduce every value.

dow-uap-pr159-historical-film-of-reporte.why: 1952 handheld 16mm Kodachrome film, not an instrumented military sensor capture; Project Blue Book's later assessments favored seabirds reflecting sunlight (DOW-UAP-D102) while war.gov's summary states the film's limited detail prevented a conclusive resolution

dow-uap-pr160-presentation-by-captain-ed.why: audio recording of a 1952 briefing by an Air Force officer, a spoken account rather than a sensor capture

dow-uap-d102-project-blue-book-file-on-t.why: the file records Project Blue Book's later assessments favoring seabirds reflecting sunlight, alongside the finding that the film alone cannot establish distance, size, altitude or speed

dow-uap-d103-project-blue-book-photo-fil.why: the file records a December 1952 pillow-balloon review and later Air Force assessments favoring seabirds, without a demonstrated identification

dow-uap-pr130-unresolved-uap-report-iraq.why: a still frame from an infrared system aboard a U.S. military platform, filed as a PDF; scored on the same sensor tier as the video captures from the same kind of platform
